findings.claim: I4 says kmctl reads and uses only spec fields plus handoff_key, but the planned test checks only the keys kmctl writes. Marking I4 enforced on that test would claim more than it pins: a reader of a non-spec key (review-due, handoffs-list, supersede, the handoff_key lookup) could be added and the test would never fire. The plan has to choose: reword I4 to the write claim the test pins, or say how the read side is pinned too.
I4's read side was not pinned. The plan now adds a read test against the same allowed-key list, so the claim and the tests match.

The read test depends on telling front matter mappings apart from other dicts, and the plan gives no rule for that. Today kmctl reads front matter in three shapes: a direct call (front_matter(path).get('status'), supersede.py:101, concepts.py:130), a variable or parameter named meta (handoffs.py:52, review_due.py:115 and :123, where meta is a plain dict parameter), and values taken out of it under other names (generated.get('at') handoffs.py:60, e.get('at') review_due.py:118, entry.get('resource') review_due.py:129). Other modules call .get on dicts that are not front matter (plugin.py:118-198 p.get('id'), m.get('name'); checks.py:285). Scanning every .get gives false failures. Scanning only front_matter(...) results misses the parameters and the nested reads, so 'fails when an unknown key is read' would hold only for the one shape the test happens to cover. The allowed list also leaves out sources[].resource, which review_due.py:129 reads. The plan has to state the rule: for example, all front matter reads go through one accessor in okf.py that the scan can find by name, or the scan follows a stated naming convention that a test also enforces. A spike can settle it: write the scan against current src/kmctl/ and check that it finds exactly stale_after, generated.at, title, description, verified[].at, sources[].resource, status and handoff_key, and nothing from plugin.py or checks.py.
I4's read side was not pinned. Resolved in round 2: a read test checks against the same allowed-key list.

The ast read scan had no rule for telling front matter apart from other dicts. Resolved: every read goes through okf.field(meta, path), which raises on keys not in the list. The scan finds field() calls by name and checks their keys, and it bans .get, subscript and `in` on front_matter(...) results. sources[].resource is now in the list. plugin.py and checks.py dicts are out of the scan because they never come from front_matter.

field() turns any truthy non-list value at a [] path into a list of one, so `sources: src/a.py` (a bare string) or a single sources mapping now yields a resource. The old _sources returned [] for any non-list sources, so review_due now checks git history for concepts it used to skip. The plan says field keeps today's forms; the single-mapping case was only meant for verified.

test_manifesto_marks_i4_enforced checks the log with r'I4.*enforced|`manifesto`' on the last dated section, and the I1/I3 line in that section already contains `manifesto`, so the test passes with the I4 log line deleted. r5's fails_when names a missing log line.

ALLOWED_FIELDS cites the wrong spec sections for two keys: the pinned validator puts `verified` under section 5.2 (5.3 is trust tiers) and root-index `okf_version` under section 12, not 8 (section 8 says a non-root index carries no front matter).

The reads scan only recognises a bare-name front_matter(...) call, so `okf.front_matter(p).get('title')` or an alias such as `fm = front_matter` reads front matter without the test noticing. Nothing in src does this today.
